title: What is RAG
text: Retrieval-augmented generation grounds a language model's answer in retrieved documents instead of relying only on its parameters. A retriever finds relevant passages for the query, and the generator conditions on them, which reduces hallucination and lets the system cite sources.

title: Pixel RAG
text: Pixel RAG skips HTML parsing entirely: it screenshots each page, slices it into tiles, and embeds the tiles with a vision-language model. This preserves tables, charts, and layout that text extraction destroys, at the cost of storage, slower indexing, and heavier GPU use.

title: Hybrid RAG
text: Hybrid RAG indexes both the extracted text and the rendered pixels of a page, then fuses the two result lists at query time. Text retrieval stays fast and cheap for code, logs, and prose, while the vision index carries tables, charts, and complex layouts.

title: Selective pixel indexing
text: A page of prose, a code listing, or a JSON dump gains nothing from a screenshot because the text index already covers it. Selective pixel indexing scores each page's visual richness and only renders, tiles, and embeds the visually rich ones, cutting storage and GPU on text-native pages.

title: Batched ingestion
text: Embedding one document at a time wastes an encoder's throughput. Batched ingestion buffers prepared chunks across many documents and embeds them in fixed-size batches while preparing the next documents on worker threads, dramatically speeding up indexing of large corpora.
